summary: Independently verified the vanish/flicker fix on /demo-trade. Sampled the [data-testid=drawing-canvas] every animation frame (rAF loop calling getImageData) while dragging the chart ~30 steps past the left-pan lock. Ran the vanish/flicker check for Rectangle, Trend Line, Horizontal Line on desktop (1920x1080, mouse drag) and Rectangle on mobile (390x844, CDP touch dispatch + fling). In every case there were ZERO blank frames between first and last painted frame, and zero painted<->blank transitions when the shape was on-screen. Additionally, at the pan-lock the drawing's leftmost opaque column stayed pinned (delta 0-2px, max frame step 0-2px) while the right-most candle column stayed pinned (delta 0px). Regression: compact style bar is visible with pen/line/eye/trash/close buttons on mobile; drawings land at the click point; drawings persist after pan through the lock.
critical_code_review_comments: geom.js fallback is correct and symmetric: x(t) adds xShift and interpolates from the visible logical range when ts.logicalToCoordinate returns null; t(x) subtracts xShift and inverts the same linear map. This keeps hit-testing consistent during over-pan attempts.
The fallback bails out (returns null) if range/span/paneW are invalid, so the previous null-return behaviour is preserved when the chart is not yet laid out.

render.js still returns null from buildGeometry() when a point has a null y (price out of view). This is intended (a drawing above/below the visible price range is skipped), and it does not cause horizontal-pan flicker because y mapping only depends on price, not on logical range.

Minor perf: the rAF loop in DrawingLayer runs continuously even when idle; it already short-circuits painting when list is empty, but calling ts.width() and getVisibleLogicalRange() every frame during idle is still measurable — could be gated on dragging/list-changed for battery on tabs left open.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Repro method that reliably exposes the pre-fix bug: (1) open [data-testid=desk-rail-drawing] (mobile-chart-tools -> rail-drawing on mobile), (2) click draw-tool-rectangle, (3) drag inside the drawing-canvas, (4) close the rail with drawings-close so canvas pointerEvents becomes 'none', (5) install a rAF loop calling canvas.getContext('2d',{willReadFrequently:true}).getImageData(0,0,W,H) and count non-transparent pixels. IMPORTANT: sample every row (y+=1) — a step of y+=2 misses thin diagonal trend lines and gives false-positive 'blank' frames. Then drag the trade-chart left in 30 steps of ~35px each with 35ms between. Data from this run: desktop rect 79/79 painted, 0 blanks; desktop trend 83/83 painted (y+=1 sampling), 0 blanks; desktop hline 78/78; mobile rect 95 painted / 199 sampled, 0 blanks between first/last painted, 1 painted<->blank transition (drawing left the visible area near end). Pan lock: dl leftmost column delta 0-2px while cand rightmost delta 0px in tail 20 frames.
rca of the issue: Before the fix, buildGeometry() returned null whenever any point's pixel could not be resolved (toPx). x(t) resolved via ts.logicalToCoordinate() which returns null once the logical index falls outside the CURRENT visible logical range. During a left-pan drag, some frames land in a state where the drawing's anchor time is just outside the visible range — so on those frames the entire shape was skipped, producing the flicker. Fix: in geom.makeConverters, x(t) and t(x) fall back to a simple linear map derived from the visible logical range (which is always finite/positive when the chart is laid out) and also apply xShift. Because the fallback still uses the same underlying (l, range) coordinate space, the fallback pixel matches ts.logicalToCoordinate() at the range boundary, so there is no seam when the fallback kicks in. This eliminates both the vanish (0 blank frames now) and the alternating blink (0 transitions). It also keeps drawing-to-candle alignment stable during the over-pan because xShift cancels the timeScale's over-pan gap consistently.
